events.title: MariaDB first released
events.summary: Michael Widenius released MariaDB 5.1.38 on October 29, 2009 — a community fork of MySQL after Oracle acquired Sun.
events.about: MariaDB stays wire-compatible with MySQL while adding storage engines (Aria, ColumnStore) and staying GPL-licensed. Linux distros (Debian, Fedora, RHEL) replaced default MySQL packages with MariaDB. Teams forked to keep an open, community-governed SQL database when Oracle owned MySQL.

narrative.whyChosen: MariaDB was Monty's answer to fears that Oracle would stall MySQL's open development.
narrative.whyImportant: It preserved a drop-in MySQL alternative adopted by major Linux distributions worldwide.
narrative.problemSolved: The MySQL community needed a fork they could trust after Sun's acquisition by Oracle.
